functions.name: bindCheckbox
functions.description: Props for Checkbox and Switch

functions.name: bindInput
functions.description: Props for the text fields with a change event: Input, Textarea and PasswordInput – `<Input {...bindInput(field)} />`. SearchField, MaskInput, PhoneInput, ColorInput, JsonInput, PinInput, Mentions and Autocomplete report their text with `onValueChange`: use bindValue

functions.name: bindValue
functions.description: Props for Select, RadioGroup, ChipGroup, SegmentedControl and the other components with `value`/`onValueChange`

functions.name: closeAllDialogs
functions.description: Closes all dialogs of the <DialogHost />; their promises resolve with undefined

functions.name: confirm
functions.description: Asks for confirmation in the app-wide <ConfirmDialog />. Resolves with true (confirmed) or false (cancelled, Escape, a newer confirm()).

functions.name: createToaster
functions.description: A toaster of its own, e.g. for a second position on the screen: `const { toaster, toast } = createToaster({ placement: 'top' })`, rendered by `<Toaster :toaster="toaster" />`.

functions.name: dateInput
functions.description: DataTable feature: the DatePicker for `date` and `datetime` filters and editors (without: the browser's date input)

functions.name: defaultBubbleTools
functions.description: Tools of the bubble menu (text selected) by default

functions.name: defaultFloatingTools
functions.description: Tools of the floating menu (empty line) by default

functions.name: defaultTools
functions.description: Tools in order; '|' draws a separator

functions.name: firstError
functions.description: First readable message of TanStack Form errors (strings or Standard Schema issues).

functions.name: navigationProgress
functions.description: Controls the app-wide <NavigationProgress />, e.g. from router events

functions.name: numberInput
functions.description: DataTable feature: the NumberInput for `number` filters and editors (without: the browser's number input)

functions.name: openDialog
functions.description: Opens content in a dialog of the app-wide <DialogHost />. Resolves with what the content passes to `close(result)`, or undefined when closed with Escape or the close button. The returned promise also has `close(result)` and `update(changes)`; dialogs opened from a dialog stack on top of it.

functions.name: prompt
functions.description: Asks for a text in the app-wide <ConfirmDialog />. Resolves with the (valid) text, or null when cancelled.

functions.name: useClipboard
functions.description: Copies text; `copied` is true for `timeout` ms afterwards (for a "Copied" state), `error` holds a failure

functions.name: useColorScheme
functions.description: The colour scheme of the system: 'light' or 'dark' ('light' on the server)

functions.name: useDebouncedCallback
functions.description: A function that runs `fn` once `wait` ms passed without another call – with `cancel`, `flush` and `pending`. Always calls the latest `fn`; cancelled when the component unmounts.

functions.name: useDebouncedValue
functions.description: A copy of `value` that follows only after `wait` ms without changes (search fields, resizing)

functions.name: useDisclosure
functions.description: Open/closed state of a dialog, drawer, menu …: `const { opened, open, close, toggle } = useDisclosure()`

functions.name: useDocumentTitle
functions.description: Sets the document title while mounted and whenever it changes

functions.name: useDocumentVisibility
functions.description: 'visible' or 'hidden' (another tab, minimised) – 'visible' on the server

functions.name: useElementSize
functions.description: Width and height of an element (content box, px; 0 until measured)

functions.name: useEyeDropper
functions.description: The EyeDropper API (Chromium): pick a colour anywhere on the screen; `open` resolves with the hex colour or null

functions.name: useFileDialog
functions.description: Opens the system's file dialog; `files` holds the last choice

functions.name: useFocusReturn
functions.description: Brings the focus back after a panel closes: remembers the focused element when `opened` turns true, focuses it again when it turns false. Returns the function that does it by hand.

functions.name: useFocusTrap
functions.description: Keeps Tab inside an element while `active` (pass `ref` to it) and focuses its first control

functions.name: useFormErrors
functions.description: The errors of a TanStack form for FormErrorSummary: one entry per touched field with an error, linked to the field; `attempts` (submit attempts) refocuses the summary on every submit: `<FormErrorSummary errors={summary.errors} focusKey={summary.attempts} />`

functions.name: useFullscreen
functions.description: Fullscreen for an element (pass `ref` to it; without one the whole page): `fullscreen` says whether it is shown in fullscreen, `toggle` switches

functions.name: useHeadroom
functions.description: Headroom: true while a header should hide (scrolling down past `offset`), false when scrolling up

functions.name: useHotkey
functions.description: One shortcut while mounted: `useHotkey('?', openHelp, { description: 'Help' })`

functions.name: useHotkeys
functions.description: Shortcuts while the component is mounted: `useHotkeys([['mod+k', openSearch, { description: 'Open search' }], ['g i', goToInbox]])`. "mod" is Strg or ⌘; space separates the steps of a sequence. Plain keys do not fire while typing in a field (see `enableInInputs`); every entry shows up in the HotkeysDialog when it has a description. `options` apply to all entries (an entry's own options win). Handlers may change on every render.

functions.name: useIdle
functions.description: Whether the user did nothing (mouse, keyboard, touch, scroll) for `timeout` ms

functions.name: useIntersection
functions.description: The IntersectionObserver entry of an element (pass `ref` to it)

functions.name: useInterval
functions.description: Runs `fn` every `interval` ms while active (starts on mount unless `autoStart: false`)

functions.name: useInViewport
functions.description: Whether an element is (partly) in the viewport (pass `ref` to it)

functions.name: useIsApple
functions.description: Whether the device is an Apple one (⌘ instead of Strg) – false on the server and during hydration

functions.name: useLandmarks
functions.description: F6 / Shift+F6 jump between the landmarks of the page while mounted (header, navigation, main, aside, toasts …)

functions.name: useLocale
functions.description: Locale, writing direction and texts of the nearest LocaleProvider – English (en-US) without one

functions.name: useLocalStorage
functions.description: A JSON value in localStorage under `key`: `[value, setValue, removeValue]`. Changes from other tabs and other components arrive; the default on the server and during hydration.

functions.name: useLongPress
functions.description: Pressing and holding (`delay` ms, default 500) calls `onLongPress` – with mouse, touch and pen. Spread the returned handlers on the element: `<button {...longPress}>`; the click that ends a long press is swallowed.

functions.name: useMediaQuery
functions.description: Whether a media query matches, e.g. `useMediaQuery('(min-width: 768px)')` – updates when it changes

functions.name: useNetwork
functions.description: Online state and connection quality (where the browser tells) – online on the server

functions.name: useRecipe
functions.description: The recipe with the defaults and classes of the nearest RecipesProvider and the component's `classes` prop

functions.name: useReducedMotion
functions.description: Whether the user asked for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)

functions.name: useRegisteredHotkeys
functions.description: The registered shortcuts (enabled, with a description), updated as components register them

functions.name: useResizeObserver
functions.description: The content box of an element as it changes (pass `ref` to it)

functions.name: useScrollSpy
functions.description: The id of the section being read: the last of `ids` whose top passed `offset` px (e.g. a sticky header) – for a table of contents

functions.name: useSelection
functions.description: Selected items of a list: toggle, select all, clear – with "all"/"some" for a header checkbox

functions.name: useSessionStorage
functions.description: Like useLocalStorage, in sessionStorage (this tab only, gone when it closes)

functions.name: useStateHistory
functions.description: A value with undo and redo: `set` adds a step, `undo`/`redo` move through them

functions.name: useThrottledCallback
functions.description: A function that runs `fn` at most once per `wait` ms (scroll, pointer move)

functions.name: useTimeout
functions.description: Runs `fn` once after `delay` ms when started (on mount with `autoStart`)

functions.name: useTranslations
functions.description: Texts of the nearest LocaleProvider

functions.name: useValidators
functions.description: The validators with the texts and number format of the nearest LocaleProvider: `const v = useValidators()`, then `validators: { onChange: v.combine(v.isRequired(), v.isEmail()) }`. Each validator is a Standard Schema, so TanStack Form takes it directly.

functions.name: useWindowScroll
functions.description: Scroll position of the window and `scrollTo` (0 on the server)

functions.name: validateFields
functions.description: Validates some fields of a TanStack form (e.g. one Wizard step) and marks them touched, so their errors show. Resolves with true when none has an error.

functions.name: virtualRows
functions.description: DataTable feature: only the visible rows are rendered with `virtual` – `<DataTable features={[virtualRows]} virtual>`

guides.title: Built into the components
guides.text:
| Topic                                | Implementation                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Contrast (1.4.3, 1.4.11)             | All token pairs ≥ 4.5:1 for text, ≥ 3:1 for borders, selected states, icons and focus – in every theme, light and dark, including hover; `checkTheme()` checks your own themes                                                          |
| Focus (2.4.7)                        | Visible focus ring (`focus-visible`) on everything that is interactive                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Labels & descriptions (1.3.1, 4.1.2) | `Field` links label, help text and error through `for`/`aria-describedby`; prefix/suffix are read out as well                                                                                                                           |
| Errors (3.3.1)                       | `error` sets `aria-invalid`, the error text is a live region                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Required fields (3.3.2)              | `required` on the input; the asterisk is `aria-hidden`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Icon buttons (4.1.2, 2.5.3)          | `label` is required and becomes the `aria-label`; a counter badge becomes part of the name (“Notifications, 4 new”); icons are always `aria-hidden`                                                                                     |
| Avatars (1.1.1)                      | With `name`: an image (`role="img"`) with the name instead of spelled-out initials; without `name`: decorative (`aria-hidden`)                                                                                                          |
| Avatar groups (1.3.1)                | `role="group"` with `label`; “+5” is announced as “5 more”                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Breadcrumb (1.3.1, 2.4.8)            | `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` with `<ol>`, separators `aria-hidden`, current page `aria-current="page"`, icon-only items keep their text for screen readers                                                                           |
| Status dots (1.4.1)                  | Never color alone – `StatusDot` always shows a text label, the dot is `aria-hidden`                                                                                                                                                     |
| Selection controls (2.1.1, 4.1.2)    | Checkbox, Switch (`role=\"switch\"`), Radio, Chips (`aria-pressed`) and segments use real inputs or buttons: Tab, Space and arrow keys as in the ARIA Authoring Practices; groups are named; the focus ring sits visibly on the control |
| High contrast for selection          | Selected chips, segments, checkboxes and switches use the system color `Highlight` in Windows contrast mode                                                                                                                             |
| Select (4.1.2, 2.1.1)                | Combobox with listbox: open with Enter/arrow, select with Enter, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger; disabled options are skipped; named through `Field`                                                                       |
| Tabs (4.1.2, 2.1.1)                  | `tablist` with a name, arrow keys/Home/End switch, the panel is focusable and named after its tab                                                                                                                                       |
| Steps (1.3.1)                        | `<ol>` with `aria-current=\"step\"`; every step announces its status (completed/current/to do)                                                                                                                                          |
| Pagination (2.4.8)                   | `<nav>` with a name, page buttons as “Page 2 of 3”, current page `aria-current=\"page\"`, the summary “5–8 of 12” is a live region                                                                                                      |
| Progress (4.1.2)                     | `progressbar` named after the label, the value as `aria-valuetext` (“68%”)                                                                                                                                                              |
| Menu (2.1.1, 4.1.2)                  | Trigger with `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`, arrow keys in the menu, Enter selects, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger                                                                                                        |
| Dialog (2.1.2, 2.4.3)                | Focus trap, `aria-modal`, named after the title and described by the description, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger; `role=\"alertdialog\"` for confirmations                                                                 |
| Tooltip (1.4.13)                     | also appears on keyboard focus, describes the trigger (`aria-describedby`), stays open on hover, Escape closes                                                                                                                          |
| Toasts (4.1.3, 2.2.1)                | named live region “Notifications”, every toast `role=\"status\"` with a close button; toasts with an action do not disappear by themselves                                                                                              |
| Loading (4.1.3)                      | A button with `loading` stays focusable (`aria-disabled`, `aria-busy`) and ignores clicks; `Spinner` is a live region                                                                                                                   |
| Alerts (4.1.3)                       | `Alert` is `role="alert"` (warn, danger) or `role="status"` (info, success)                                                                                                                                                             |
| Target size (2.5.8)                  | All controls at least 24 × 24 px                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Motion (2.3.3)                       | Overlays fade in and out smoothly (Dialog, Menu, Select, Tooltip, Toasts); with `prefers-reduced-motion` there are no animations and a slower spinner – the keyboard tests run in both variants                                         |
| High contrast mode                   | Buttons and badges show an outline in Windows contrast mode (`forced-colors`)                                                                                                                                                           |

guides.title: What stays with the project
guides.text:
- Every input needs a name: `Field` with `label` – or `aria-label` on the `Input`.
- Render clickable cards with `asChild` as `<a>` or `<button>`, never as a clickable `<div>`.
- Add router links (RouterLink, Next.js Link) to the breadcrumb through `BreadcrumbItem` with `asChild`.
- If a `StatusDot` changes live, give the element `role="status"` so that the change is announced.
- Default texts (`Loading`, `Close`) come from the `LocaleProvider` (English without a provider, e.g. German with `locale="de-DE"` after `registerLocale('de', de)`); single texts can be overridden through props like `label` / `dismissLabel`.
- Set `lang` and `dir` on the `<html>` element – screen readers choose the pronunciation from it, browsers the writing direction.
- Set the focus sensibly after an `Alert` is closed.

guides.title: Automated checks
guides.text:
```sh
docker compose run --rm workspace pnpm test   # token contrasts + axe in jsdom (Vue and React)
docker compose run --rm a11y                  # axe in a real browser against every story, light + dark
```

guides.title: Installation
guides.text:
The packages are published on npm:

```sh
pnpm add @wirecore/wirelayer-vue    # or
pnpm add @wirecore/wirelayer-react  # or
pnpm add @wirecore/wirelayer-native
```

guides.title: Adding the styles
Usage
guides.text:
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Button, Field, Input } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue';
import { ArrowRight } from '@lucide/vue';
</script>

<template>
    <Field label="Email" required>
        <Input v-model="email" type="email" />
    </Field>
    <Button :trailing-icon="ArrowRight">Start project</Button>
</template>
```

```tsx
import { Button, Field, Input } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-react';
import { ArrowRight } from 'lucide-react';

<Field label="Email" required>
    <Input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
</Field>
<Button trailingIcon={ArrowRight}>Start project</Button>
```

guides.title: Nuxt
Next.js (App Router)
Light, dark and themes
guides.text:
Light/dark is switched by the `data-mode` attribute, the color theme by the `data-theme` attribute – e.g. on the
`<html>` element:

```html
<html data-mode="dark" data-theme="ocean"></html>
```

Without `data-mode` the page follows the system setting (`prefers-color-scheme`) – light or dark, without any
JavaScript. `data-mode="light"` or `data-mode="dark"` forces a mode, also for a part of the page. Without `data-theme`
the theme “WireLayer” (`data-theme="wirecore"`) applies. With Tailwind you can style specifically with `dark:` – it
follows the same rules. More under _Foundations › Themes_.

guides.title: Customizing: defaults and classes per part
guides.text:
Every component consists of named parts of its recipe (`base`, `icon`, `row`, `trigger` …, see
`@wirecore/wirelayer-recipes`). `RecipesProvider` sets default variants and additional classes for everything below it
(inner providers extend outer ones), the `classes` prop adds classes for a single component. Explicitly set props and
`class`/`className` always win; classes are merged with tailwind-merge.

```vue
<RecipesProvider
    :recipes="{
        button: { defaultVariants: { size: 'sm' }, classes: { base: 'tracking-wide' } },
        dataTable: { defaultVariants: { size: 'sm' }, classes: { th: 'bg-bg-2' } },
    }"
>
    <App />
</RecipesProvider>

<Button :classes="{ icon: 'text-primary' }" :leading-icon="Plus">New</Button>
```

```tsx
<RecipesProvider recipes={{ card: { classes: { base: 'rounded-none' } } }}>
    <App />
</RecipesProvider>;

<DataTable classes={{ row: 'h-14' }} … />;
```

The names are the exports of the recipes (`button`, `iconButton`, `dataTable` …) and are checked by TypeScript, as are
the variants and parts. Your own components use the same through `useRecipe('button', button)`.

`variants` adds classes for single values of a variant, `compoundVariants` for combinations – instead of selectors on
the recipe's own classes, which break when they change:

```ts
const recipes: RecipeConfig = {
    // only the medium size: 42px high, 16px text
    button: {
        variants: { size: { md: { base: 'h-[2.625rem] text-base' } } },
        compoundVariants: [{ size: ['sm', 'md'], shape: 'rounded', classes: { base: 'rounded-md' } }],
    },
    input: { variants: { size: { md: { base: 'h-[2.625rem]' } }, invalid: { true: { base: 'border-2' } } } },
};
```

Per part the classes come in this order: `classes`, the matching `variants` and `compoundVariants`, the states of the
recipe, the overrides of states (`invalid: { true: … }`), and last the class passed to the component. Inner providers
extend outer ones (classes of the same value are joined, the inner ones win).

Classes from a provider or `classes` change the look, not the states: the classes of an active state variant
(`invalid`, `success`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `current`, `selected`, `checked`, `loading`) are added after them, so a
field with `classes: { base: 'border-line-2' }` still turns red when it is invalid. States that the components mark as
attributes (`data-invalid:`, `data-disabled:`, `data-[state=checked]:`) win through their selector anyway. Only the
class passed to the component itself (`class`/`className`) comes after the states – the way out when a single field
should look different in every state.

guides.title: Hooks and composables
guides.text:
Around 40 hooks (React) and composables (Vue) with the same names and the same logic – for your own components and
pages: state (`useDisclosure`, `useSelection`, `useStateHistory`), time (`useDebouncedValue`, `useInterval`, `useIdle`),
browser (`useClipboard`, `useLocalStorage`, `useMediaQuery`, `useReducedMotion`, `useFullscreen`), observers
(`useElementSize`, `useIntersection`, `useScrollSpy`), focus (`useFocusTrap`, `useFocusReturn`) and keyboard shortcuts
(`useHotkeys`, shown in the `HotkeysDialog`). Examples: _Utilities › Hooks_ in the
Vue and React Storybooks; React Native has a subset with the same names.

```ts
import { useDisclosure, useLocalStorage } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue'; // or @wirecore/wirelayer-react

const { opened, open, close } = useDisclosure();
const note = useLocalStorage('note', ''); // React: const [note, setNote] = useLocalStorage('note', '')
```

guides.title: Blocks and ConditionBuilder
guides.text:
`@wirecore/wirelayer-blocks-vue` and `@wirecore/wirelayer-blocks-react` build on `@wirecore/wirelayer-vue` and `@wirecore/wirelayer-react`
(peer dependency) and bring larger building blocks: SiteHeader, CtaSection, ModeToggle, AuthForm, AuthLayout and the
ConditionBuilder (nested AND/OR rules). Examples: _Blocks_ in the Vue and React Storybooks.

```sh
pnpm add @wirecore/wirelayer-blocks-vue    # or @wirecore/wirelayer-blocks-react
```

The ConditionBuilder is also the editor for the advanced filter of the DataTable. The table filters by itself (or passes
the tree to the server as `condition`); it gets the editor from outside – without it, it shows no button and points this
out on the console during development:

```tsx
import { ConditionBuilder } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-blocks-react';
import { DataTable } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-react/data-table';

<DataTable
    data={rows}
    columns={columns}
    advancedFilter
    renderAdvancedFilter={(props) => <ConditionBuilder {...props} />}
/>;
```

```vue
<DataTable :data="rows" :columns="columns" advanced-filter>
    <template #advancedFilter="{ fields, value, setValue, label }">
        <ConditionBuilder :fields="fields" :model-value="value" :label="label" @update:model-value="setValue" />
    </template>
</DataTable>
```

guides.title: DataTable feature modules
guides.text:
Parts of the DataTable that bring a lot of code along are imported on their own – an app only bundles the ones it passes
in `features` (fixed for the life of a table). The DatePicker alone is about 40 KB (gzip).

| Feature       | Import                                                                 | Adds                                                 | Without it                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `virtualRows` | `@wirecore/wirelayer-react/virtual` (peer dependency TanStack Virtual) | only the visible rows are rendered with `virtual`    | all rows are rendered, a hint in development |
| `dateInput`   | `@wirecore/wirelayer-react/data-table`                                 | DatePicker for `date` and `datetime` filters/editors | the browser's date input                     |
| `numberInput` | `@wirecore/wirelayer-react/data-table`                                 | NumberInput for `number` filters and editors         | the browser's number input                   |

```tsx
import { DataTable, dateInput, numberInput } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-react/data-table';
import { virtualRows } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-react/virtual';

// Once for all tables of the app
const features = [virtualRows, dateInput, numberInput];

<DataTable data={rows} columns={columns} features={features} scrollHeight="480px" virtual />;
```

```vue
<DataTable :data="rows" :columns="columns" :features="features" scroll-height="480px" virtual />
```

Vue: the same imports from `@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/data-table` and `@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/virtual`.

guides.title: AI assistants (MCP, llms.txt)
guides.text:
So that Claude, Cursor and others use the components correctly, the API is available as text and as an MCP server:

- **`/llms.txt`** and **`/llms-full.txt`** in this Storybook: an overview and all props (React and Vue names),
  hooks and these guides in one file.
- **In every package** (`@wirecore/wirelayer-vue`, `-react`, `-native`, `-css`): `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` in that
  package's own syntax – Vue with events and slots, HTML as a class reference. Point the assistant at
  `node_modules/@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/llms.txt` (e.g. in CLAUDE.md); they match the installed version.
- **MCP server** `@wirecore/wirelayer-mcp` with the tools `list_components`, `get_component`, `search_components` and
  `get_guide`:

```sh
claude mcp add wirelayer -- npx -y -p @wirecore/wirelayer-mcp wirelayer-mcp
```

The package is called `@wirecore/wirelayer-mcp`, the command `wirelayer-mcp` (the former name `wirecore-mcp` still works).

Both are generated from the source code (`pnpm --filter @wirecore/wirelayer-mcp collect`); a test checks that they are
up to date.

guides.title: Language and writing direction
guides.text:
By default the components speak English (`en-US`). `LocaleProvider` switches texts, number and date formats and the
writing direction for everything below it – English is built in; other languages are registered once (see below),
get their texts through `translations` or fall back to English:

```vue
<LocaleProvider locale="de-DE"><!-- after registerLocale('de', de) -->
    <App />
</LocaleProvider>
```

```tsx
import { messages } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-recipes';

<LocaleProvider locale="fr-FR" translations={{ ...messages.en, common: { ...messages.en.common, close: 'Fermer' } }}>
    <App />
</LocaleProvider>;
```

The app sets `lang` and `dir` on the `<html>` element itself. For languages like Arabic or Hebrew (`dir="rtl"`),
spacing, borders, directional icons and the arrow keys are mirrored. Your own components read the texts with
`useTranslations()` and the locale and direction with `useLocale()`. In Storybook the **Language** toolbar item
switches between English and the registered languages (Arabic also shows the right-to-left layout).

### Registering languages

German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Portugal and Brazil), Dutch, Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Latvian, Arabic
and Turkish ship as separate modules – they cost nothing as long as an app does not import them. Registered once at
startup, they apply to every region of the language (`fr` also for `fr-CA`):

```ts
import { registerLocale } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue'; // likewise @wirecore/wirelayer-react and @wirecore/wirelayer-native
import { ar } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/locales/ar';
import { de } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/locales/de';
import { fr } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/locales/fr';
import { ptBR } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/locales/pt-BR';

registerLocale('de', de); // de-DE, de-AT, de-CH …
registerLocale('fr', fr);
registerLocale('ar', ar); // ar-EG, ar-MA … – right to left
registerLocale('pt-BR', ptBR); // a region takes precedence over its language (pt)
```

Instead of registering, a module can also be passed directly: `<LocaleProvider locale="fr-FR" :translations="fr">`.
Plurals follow the rules of the language (`Intl.PluralRules`, e.g. the six forms of Arabic), numbers in the texts
follow the locale (`ar-EG` writes Arabic-Indic digits, `de-DE` only groups from 10.000 on). The texts should be proofread by
native speakers before use.

guides.title: Server data and loading more
guides.text:
Components with lists, pages or parts that load later support two ways – both with the same names:

- **Manual:** the app loads by itself and passes the result in (`items`, `data`, `events` …). The component reports
  what it needs – `filterChange` (search text), `loadMore` (end reached), `pageChange`, `loadChildren`,
  `rangeChange` – and shows the state with `loading`, `hasMore` and `totalCount`/`rowCount`. When the server searches,
  `manualFilter` prevents a second filtering in the browser.
- **Data source:** with `dataSource` and `getItems`, the component asks by itself – the first page when it opens, a
  search after a typing pause, further pages while scrolling. Outdated requests are canceled, loading and results are
  announced, errors are shown with “Try again”. `getChildren` loads children in trees, `getItemsByKeys` the labels of
  selected values that are not loaded (yet). Nothing is requested on the server.

```ts
import type { DataSource } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-recipes';

export const customers: DataSource<Customer> = {
    async getItems({ page = 1, pageSize = 50, search = '', signal }) {
        const query = new URLSearchParams({ page: String(page), size: String(pageSize), q: search });
        const response = await fetch(`/api/customers?${query}`, { signal });
        const { rows, total } = await response.json();
        return { items: rows, totalCount: total };
    },
};
```

```vue
<Select v-model="customer" :data-source="customers" filter :min-search-length="2" item-value="id" item-label="name" />
```

| Component                                              | Manual                                                        | `dataSource`                                 | Loading more                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Select, MultiSelect, Combobox, Autocomplete, Listbox   | `filterChange`, `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore`              | ✓                                            | at the end of the list               |
| VirtualSelect, TagsInput (suggestions)                 | like Select                                                   | ✓                                            | at the end of the list               |
| Mentions                                               | `search`, `loading`                                           | ✓ (per trigger)                              | –                                    |
| CommandPalette                                         | `filterChange`, `loading`, `filter: false`                    | ✓ (after its own matches)                    | –                                    |
| VirtualList                                            | `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore`                              | ✓                                            | while scrolling                      |
| DataView                                               | `manual`, `totalCount`, `pageChange`, `loadMore`, `loading`   | ✓ (pages or infinite)                        | pages, “Load more”, scrolling        |
| DataTable                                              | `manual`, `rowCount`, sorting/filter/page, `loadMore`         | ✓ (also the advanced filter as `condition`)  | pages, scrolling (virtual)           |
| Tree, VirtualTree, TreeSelect, CascadeSelect, OrgChart | `loadChildren` (event)                                        | ✓ (`getChildren`) or `loadChildren` function | children when expanded               |
| PickList                                               | source list: `filterChange`, `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore` | –                                            | source list at the end               |
| NotificationCenter                                     | `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore`, `unreadCount`               | ✓                                            | “Load more”                          |
| LogViewer                                              | `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore`                              | ✓ (older lines)                              | “Load older entries”                 |
| Timeline, ChatMessages                                 | `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore`                              | –                                            | “Load more” or older ones at the top |
| Kanban                                                 | `loadMore` (per column), `hasMore`/`loading` of the column    | – (cards are app state)                      | “Load more” per column               |
| Gallery                                                | `loadMore`, `loading`, `hasMore`                              | –                                            | at the last two images               |
| Scheduler                                              | `rangeChange`, `loading`                                      | ✓ (`range` of the view)                      | date range when paging               |
| Gantt                                                  | `loading`                                                     | – (tasks are app state)                      | –                                    |
| Pagination, Carousel                                   | `count`, `pageChange`                                         | –                                            | –                                    |

Older names remain as aliases: `endReached`/`loadingMore` (VirtualList), `scrollEnd` (DataTable) and `search`
(CommandPalette) correspond to `loadMore`, `loading` and `filterChange`. In React the events are called `onLoadMore`,
`onFilterChange` …

guides.title: PDF viewer
guides.text:
`PdfViewer` (`@wirecore/wirelayer-vue/pdf`, `@wirecore/wirelayer-react/pdf`) shows PDFs with [pdf.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/):
pages with a text layer (selection, search, screen readers), links, the structure of tagged PDFs, toolbar, thumbnails,
table of contents, password prompt, printing and download. `pdfjs-dist` is an optional peer dependency
(**Apache-2.0** – compatible with MIT projects; keep the license text when shipping pdf.js). The legacy build of pdf.js
is used (older Safari and Firefox versions).

```sh
pnpm add pdfjs-dist
```

Set up once: the pdf.js stylesheet (`pdfjs-dist/legacy/web/pdf_viewer.css`, text and link layer) and the
worker URL (`pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs`). With Vite (Nuxt as well):

```ts
import 'pdfjs-dist/legacy/web/pdf_viewer.css';
import workerSrc from 'pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs?url';
```

```vue
<PdfViewer src="/contract.pdf" :worker-src="workerSrc" v-model:page="page" height="80vh" />
```

Next.js (webpack/Turbopack) – in a `'use client'` file:

```tsx
import 'pdfjs-dist/legacy/web/pdf_viewer.css';
import { PdfViewer } from '@wirecore/wirelayer-react/pdf';

const workerSrc = new URL('pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs', import.meta.url).toString();

<PdfViewer src="/contract.pdf" workerSrc={workerSrc} page={page} onPageChange={setPage} />;
```

Alternatively, copy the file to `public/` (`workerSrc="/pdf.worker.min.mjs"`). For fonts that are not embedded in the
PDF, copy the folders `pdfjs-dist/standard_fonts/` and `pdfjs-dist/cmaps/` to `public/` and pass them as
`standardFontDataUrl="/pdfjs/standard_fonts/"` and `cMapUrl="/pdfjs/cmaps/"` (with a trailing slash).

pdf.js runs only in the browser: the component loads it after mounting and renders the loading state on the
server – it is SSR-safe. If you do not want pdf.js code in the server bundle at all, wrap the viewer in
`<ClientOnly>` in Nuxt, and use `dynamic(() => import('./Viewer'), { ssr: false })` in Next.

guides.title: React Native (Expo)
HTML and server templates
guides.text:
`@wirecore/wirelayer-css` provides all components as `.wc-*` classes – one stylesheet, no build pipeline needed:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/wirecore/wirecore.css" />
<button type="button" class="wc-button wc-button-danger wc-button-sm">Delete</button>
```

Class scheme, examples and what works without JavaScript: _HTML / CSS › HTML › Getting started_.

guides.title: License
guides.text:
WireLayer is licensed under the MIT license. The fonts shipped with `@wirecore/wirelayer-css` (Schibsted Grotesk,
JetBrains Mono) are licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`dist/fonts/OFL.txt`). Optional peer dependencies such
as `pdfjs-dist` (Apache-2.0), Chart.js, Tiptap and Shiki are installed by the app itself – with their own licenses.

guides.title: Components and APIs side by side
guides.text:
| PrimeVue                                                                            | WireLayer                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Button label icon="pi pi-x">`                                                     | the label as slot text, `:leading-icon` with a Lucide component (`@lucide/vue`)                                   |
| `severity` / `text` / `outlined`                                                    | `color` – or `variant="text"` / `variant="outline"`                                                               |
| Icon button + `v-tooltip`                                                           | `<Tooltip content><IconButton :icon label /></Tooltip>` – `label` is the accessible name (often the tooltip text) |
| `Button :loading`                                                                   | `loading` on `Button` and `IconButton` (stays focusable, ignores clicks)                                          |
| `Card` with `#title`/`#content`                                                     | `Card` with the default slot and an own heading                                                                   |
| `InputText`, `Password`, `InputNumber`, `InputChips`, `SelectButton`, `RadioButton` | `Input`, `PasswordInput`, `NumberInput`, `TagsInput`, `SegmentedControl`, `RadioGroup` + `RadioGroupItem`         |
| `IconField` + `InputIcon`                                                           | `Input :leading-icon`                                                                                             |
| `Select :options optionLabel optionValue`                                           | `Select :items item-label item-value` (object values: `value-key`)                                                |
| `Message severity`                                                                  | `Alert status` (`error` → `danger`)                                                                               |
| `Tag`                                                                               | `Badge`                                                                                                           |
| `Dialog v-model:visible header`                                                     | `Dialog v-model:open` + `DialogContent title size` (`hide-title` keeps the title for screen readers only)         |
| `Toolbar` as a container                                                            | a plain `div` – WireLayer's `Toolbar` is `role="toolbar"` (one tab stop, arrow keys)                              |
| `useToast().add({ severity, summary, detail, life })`                               | `toast({ type, title, description, duration })`, `<Toaster />` once in the app                                    |
| `useConfirm().require({ … })`                                                       | `await confirm({ title, description, … })`, `<ConfirmDialog />` once in the app                                   |
| `DataTable` + `Column`                                                              | `DataTable :columns` (column objects), `#cell-<id>`, `#expansion`, `v-model:page-size`                            |
| `expandedRows` with a row toggler on some rows                                      | `#expansion` + `row-expandable`                                                                                   |
| `paginatorTemplate` (first/last page)                                               | `paginator-edges`, `paginator-align`                                                                              |
| `showGridlines` (with the outer border)                                             | `gridlines` + `bordered`                                                                                          |
| `FilterMatchMode`, `filters`                                                        | `v-model:global-filter`, column `filter`/`filterOptions`, `filter-display="row"`                                  |
| `@primevue/forms` + `zodResolver`                                                   | TanStack Form with Zod directly as a Standard Schema, `FormField` + `bindInput`/`bindValue`                       |
| `pt` (pass-through)                                                                 | `classes` per part, `RecipesProvider` for all components below it                                                 |
| Theme preset (`definePreset`)                                                       | `--wc-*` tokens, `defineTheme`, the component variables (_Foundations › Themes_)                                  |
| `darkModeSelector` (a class)                                                        | `data-mode` on `<html>`                                                                                           |
| `tailwindcss-primeui` (`bg-surface-*`, `text-muted-color`)                          | semantic tokens: `bg-card`, `bg-bg-2`, `text-muted`, `border-line` …                                              |

guides.title: Pitfalls
guides.text:
- **An empty choice is `null`, not `''`.** For PrimeVue's Select `''` means "nothing chosen"; WireLayer's Select treats
  `''` as a value (it warns in development that it is not among the items). Use `null`.
- **TanStack fields start with `''`.** A required text in Zod therefore needs `.min(1)` – `z.string()` alone accepts
  the empty field.
- **Fonts:** set your own with `@theme { --font-sans: … }`. Import `theme.css` instead of `styles.css` (with the
  sources files, or the Vite plugin `@wirecore/wirelayer-recipes/vite`) so the WireLayer fonts are not bundled
  (_Getting started › Welcome › Smaller CSS_).
- **Card spacing:** `Card` puts a `gap` between its direct children – wrap content that should sit tight in one
  element.
- **Overrides go per part and per variant.** `classes: { base: 'rounded-md' }` reaches every size; only the medium size
  with `variants: { size: { md: { base: '…' } } }` – no selectors on the recipe's own classes. States such as `invalid`
  stay visible over such classes; only `class` on the component itself replaces them.
- **Sizes and corners in one place:** the height, text and corners of buttons and fields per size, the corners of
  rounded buttons, the padding of cards and the backdrop of dialogs are CSS variables (`--wc-control-h-md` …).
- **Labels:** wrap a control in `Field` (it links label, description and error). A native `<label for>` works with the
  control's own `id`; date fields, sliders and groups need `Field` or `aria-label`.
- **Brand colours:** `checkTheme` lists the pairs below WCAG AA, `suggestThemeFixes` the nearest colours (and `on-*`
  colours) that meet them – an orange `primary` with white text, common in PrimeVue themes, does not.

guides.title: Custom theme
Component sizes and shapes
guides.text:
Besides the colors, a few measures that a brand usually changes are CSS variables. Without them every component looks as
before – their defaults are the values of the recipes. Set them on `:root` (all pages), on a `[data-theme]` or on any
element (that part of the page):

```css
:root {
    --wc-control-h-md: 2.625rem; /* buttons and fields of the medium size: 42px */
    --wc-control-text-md: 1rem;
    --wc-control-radius-md: 0.375rem;
    --wc-button-radius: 0.375rem;
    --wc-card-p: 1.25rem;
    --wc-backdrop: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4);
}
```

| Variable                                              | Default                    | Applies to                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--wc-control-h-sm` / `-md` / `-lg`                   | `2rem` / `2.5rem` / `3rem` | Height of the sizes sm, md, lg: Button, IconButton, Input, NativeSelect, Select, MultiSelect, Combobox, NumberInput, PasswordInput, the date and time fields, ColorPicker, TagsInput (minimum) |
| `--wc-control-radius-sm` / `-md` / `-lg`              | `6px` / `8px` / `10px`     | Corners of the fields above and of Textarea (not of buttons)                                                                                                                                   |
| `--wc-control-text-sm` / `-md` / `-lg`                | `13px` / `15px` / `16px`   | Text in the fields above and in Textarea                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--wc-button-radius`                                  | `8px`                      | Corners of Button and IconButton with `shape="rounded"` (`pill` and `square` stay)                                                                                                             |
| `--wc-card-p`                                         | `1.5rem`                   | Padding of Card                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--wc-backdrop`                                       | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6)`         | Dimming behind Dialog, Drawer and ConfirmDialog                                                                                                                                                |
| `--radius-card` / `--radius-panel` / `--radius-popup` | `20px` / `28px` / `12px`   | Corners of cards, panels and popups (menus, lists, popovers)                                                                                                                                   |
| `--wc-dialog-w`                                       | by `size`                  | Width of a DialogContent                                                                                                                                                                       |

The rest – the padding of a dialog or of table cells, the size of a single variant – is set per part with `classes` or
`RecipesProvider` (_Getting started › Welcome › Customizing_). The React Native components keep their fixed sizes.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Sections that open and close; each heading is a button with aria-expanded

props.name: value
props.description: Open items

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several items open at once

props.name: collapsible
props.description: The open item can be closed again (single mode, default true)

components.name: AccordionItem
components.description: One section of an Accordion: a heading with a button (aria-expanded) and its content; own actions beside it

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon component before the title

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Level of the heading around the trigger, to fit the screen outline (default 3)

props.name: actions
props.description: Own controls next to the heading (e.g. an IconButton) – beside the trigger, not inside it

components.name: ActionBar
components.description: Bar with the actions for selected items (e.g. in a list): the count is announced when it changes

props.name: count
props.description: Number of selected items – the bar shows while it is above 0

props.name: open
props.description: Shows the bar independently of `count`

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the toolbar (default "Actions for the selection")

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the clear button (default "Clear selection")

props.name: placement
props.description: `fixed` (default) floats above the bottom of the screen, `inline` stays in the layout

props.name: onClear
props.description: Clears the selection – shows the clear button

props.name: children
props.description: The actions, e.g. Buttons or IconButtons

components.name: AiLabel
components.description: Marks content made by AI, with an explanation behind an info button

props.name: label
props.description: Text of the label (default "AI-generated")

props.name: explanation
props.description: Text behind the (i) button; `false` hides the button

props.name: children
props.description: Content of the explanation instead of `explanation`

components.name: Alert
components.description: Message box with status icon and colour, title and text; announced when it appears (alert for warn/danger, status otherwise)

props.name: variant
props.description: `box` (default) or `simple`: only icon and text in the status colour, e.g. for a field error

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Shows a close button that calls `onDismiss`

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button

props.name: duration
props.description: Calls `onDismiss` after this many milliseconds

components.name: AppShell
components.description: Frame of an app screen without a router: header with menu button (when there is a navbar), content and an optional bottom bar; the navbar opens as a drawer. Header and footer stay, the content fills the rest.

props.name: header
props.description: Content of the header bar, e.g. the title and actions

props.name: navbar
props.description: The navigation (e.g. a SidebarNav) – in a drawer from the left behind the menu button of the header

props.name: footer
props.description: Bar at the bottom, e.g. a BottomNavigation with `inline`

props.name: navbarLabel
props.description: Title of the navigation drawer (default "Navigation")

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's content (wrap it in a ScrollView when it scrolls)

components.name: AspectRatio
components.description: Keeps the ratio of width and height, e.g. for images, videos and maps

props.name: ratio
props.description: Width ÷ height (default 16/9)

components.name: Autocomplete
components.description: Free text with suggestions below the field (in the page flow, no overlay): typing filters them, a tap takes one; on the web the arrow keys move and Enter takes the highlighted one. Any other text is allowed, too.

props.name: items
props.description: Suggestions while typing – any other text is allowed, too; strings or objects (read with itemLabel)

props.name: value
props.description: The text

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several entries as chips (a TagsInput with these suggestions) – use values/onValuesChange

props.name: values
props.description: The entries with `multiple`

props.name: max
props.description: Most entries with `multiple`

props.name: filter
props.description: Filters the suggestions by the typed text (ignores case and accents, default true)

props.name: manualFilter
props.description: The suggestions are filtered elsewhere (server): no local filtering, listen to onFilterChange

props.name: onFilterChange
props.description: Typed text – e.g. to load matching suggestions from a server (manualFilter)

props.name: itemLabel
props.description: Text of a suggestion: property name or function (default: `label`, or the item itself)

props.name: itemDisabled
props.description: Disabled state of a suggestion: property name or function (default: `disabled`)

props.name: clearable
props.description: Button that clears the text

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner in the field and "Loading" in the list (aria-busy)

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Text of the loading row in the list

props.name: hasMore
props.description: More suggestions can be loaded: "Load more" calls onLoadMore

props.name: dataSource
props.description: Loads the suggestions for the typed text (after a typing pause, outdated answers dropped)

props.name: minSearchLength
props.description: Fewest characters typed before the data source is asked

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Suggestions per request of the data source (default 50)

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Content of a suggestion (instead of its text)

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name without a surrounding Field

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Image, initials (from the name) or an icon – one image named by `name` for screen readers

props.name: name
props.description: Person or organisation – accessible name of the avatar and source of the initials

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL; initials (or the icon) are shown while it loads or if it fails

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon shown when there is neither an image nor a name (default: user icon)

props.name: color
props.description: Tinted background in a token colour; `auto` picks one from the name, so the same person always gets the same colour

components.name: Badge
components.description: Small label for a state or count, optionally with an icon or round (`circle`)

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon component rendered before the text

props.name: circle
props.description: Round shape for a count or a single character (grows into a pill for longer content)

components.name: Banner
components.description: Notice across the screen or above the content, e.g. maintenance or a missing confirmation: the text is a live region (danger: alert, else status). Without `storageKey` of the web – the app remembers the dismissal itself.

props.name: title
props.description: Bold text before the message

props.name: position
props.description: `inline` (default) in the layout, `top`/`bottom` over that edge of the screen

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Shows a close button

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: The close button was pressed – e.g. to remember the dismissal in the app's storage

props.name: icon
props.description: Own icon component instead of the one of the variant

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button (default "Dismiss notice")

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons after the message

props.name: children
props.description: The message

components.name: BarChart
components.description: Bars per category for one or more series – vertical or horizontal, grouped or stacked – drawn with react-native-svg. An image named by the title and the trend of each series; tapping shows the values of a category, the data list below is the text alternative.

props.name: data
props.description: The rows: one object per category with a value per series

props.name: categoryKey
props.description: Property of each row with the category (x axis)

props.name: series
props.description: The series: key of the value, label, colour, stack, dashed … (one value axis – `axis: 'end'` and `type` of the web's CompositeChart are not drawn)

props.name: title
props.description: Title of the chart, also the start of its accessible name

props.name: hideTitle
props.description: Keep the title for screen readers only

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the plot in pt (default 220)

props.name: table
props.description: The data as a list below the chart (opens on demand) – the text alternative (default true)

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats values in the axis, legend and data list (default: numbers in the locale)

props.name: references
props.description: Reference lines (`value`) and areas (`from`–`to`) on the value axis, or with `axis: 'x'` on the categories (index of the row); also listed as text below the chart

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend (default: with more than one series)

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Bars from the start edge instead of from the bottom

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stack all series

components.name: BarsList
components.description: A list of labels and values; the bars behind the labels show the values as lengths

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the list (visible with `showTitle`)

props.name: max
props.description: Value of a full bar (default: the largest value)

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour of the bars (default primary)

props.name: labelHeader
props.description: Column headings above the list, e.g. "Page" and "Views"

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the values (default: numbers in the locale)

components.name: BottomNavigation
components.description: Tab bar at the bottom of the screen for the main destinations of an app: screen readers hear tabs with the selected one ("Tab, 2 of 4"), badges are part of the name. No router dependency – `onNavigate` navigates.

props.name: items
props.description: 3–5 destinations

props.name: maxItems

props.name: moreLabel

components.name: BulletChart

props.name: label
props.description: Name of the measure, e.g. "Revenue" – the accessible name

props.name: description
props.description: Smaller text below the name, e.g. the unit

props.name: max

props.name: min

props.name: ranges

props.name: tone

props.name: formatValue

components.name: Button
components.description: Button with variants and colours, sizes, icons, loading state (busy, still focusable) and an optional counter

props.name: color

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner shape: `pill` (default), `rounded` or `square`

props.name: block

props.name: leadingIcon

props.name: trailingIcon

props.name: loading

props.name: badge

props.name: badgeLabel

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.description: Buttons joined into one control (role "group"): only the outer corners stay round, also stacked

props.name: label

props.name: orientation
props.description: Buttons side by side (default) or stacked

props.name: block
props.description: Full width of the container; the buttons share it

props.name: children
props.description: Button or IconButton elements

components.name: Calendar

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (ISO or Date)

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (ISO or Date)

props.name: isDateUnavailable
props.description: Dates that cannot be chosen, e.g. weekends – receives the ISO date

props.name: excludeDates
props.description: Single dates that cannot be chosen (holidays, booked days)

props.name: showWeekNumbers
props.description: Column with the ISO calendar weeks ("Wk")

props.name: showButtonBar
props.description: "Today" and "Clear" below the calendar

props.name: highlightToday
props.description: Today is bold and underlined (default true)

props.name: hideOutsideDays
props.description: Leaves the days of the previous and next month empty

props.name: firstDayOfWeek
props.description: First day of the week: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday; default from the locale

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA zone that decides which day is today

props.name: value
props.description: ISO date, e.g. "2026-10-20" (a Date is accepted too)

props.name: valueType
props.description: What onValueChange gets: ISO strings (default) or Date objects

props.name: defaultMonth
props.description: Month shown first (ISO) – default: the value or today

props.name: allowDeselect
props.description: Choosing the selected day again clears it

components.name: Card
components.description: Surface for grouped content – with title, subtitle, media and footer, or any children; pressable with `onPress`

props.name: onPress
props.description: Makes the whole card pressable (role "button" unless set otherwise)

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the card

props.name: subtitle

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Level of the title heading – pick the one that fits the screen outline (default 3)

props.name: media
props.description: Image or video above the content (beside it when horizontal) – reaches the edges of the card

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal`: media at the start, the content beside it

props.name: header
props.description: Extra content in the header, after the title (e.g. a Badge or an IconButton)

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions at the end of the card

components.name: Carousel
components.description: Slides to swipe through (FlatList with paging): arrow buttons, dots, autoplay with pause (WCAG 2.2.2), the arrow keys on the web. Slides outside the page are hidden from screen readers; iOS and Android announce the new slide.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the carousel

props.name: children
props.description: Renders one slide

props.name: slidesPerPage
props.description: Slides visible at once (default 1); fractions show part of the next one

props.name: slidesToScroll
props.description: Slides per step (default a page)

props.name: breakpoints
props.description: Settings by the width of the carousel

props.name: spacing
props.description: Space between the slides in pt (default 16)

props.name: loop
props.description: After the last page comes the first

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Turns the pages by itself (default every 4 s) – always with a pause button, not with reduced motion

props.name: indicators
props.description: Dots, one per page (default true)

components.name: CascadeSelect
components.description: Select with cascading levels: the trigger shows the whole path and opens a sheet with one level at a time – a radio group per level, an option with children opens the next level, "Back" goes up; the path is the subtitle. With `filter` a search lists the hits with their path.

props.name: value
props.description: Chosen value; any type (see `valueKey`)

props.name: title
props.description: Title of the sheet – default: the Field label or the placeholder

props.name: separator
props.description: Separator of the path shown in the field and in the sheet ("Germany › Bavaria › Munich")

props.name: valueKey
props.description: Identifies object values (property name or function), e.g. "id" – without it objects are compared by content

props.name: changeOnSelect
props.description: The levels in between can be chosen, too (first entry of each level: "Choose <level>")

props.name: filter
props.description: Search field in the sheet: the hits are listed with their whole path

props.name: clearable
props.description: Button next to the field that clears the value

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the clear button (default "Clear selection")

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner in the field (busy)

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the field: 32, 40 (default) or 48 pt

props.name: loadChildren
props.description: Loads the options of a level (`hasChildren: true`) when it opens; the signal aborts it

props.name: onLoadChildren
props.description: A lazy level opened and there is no loadChildren/dataSource: add its options to the items

props.name: dataSource
props.description: Source of the options of lazy levels (`getChildren`)

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name without a surrounding Field

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the sheet's close button

components.name: Center
components.description: Centres its content horizontally and vertically

props.name: inline
props.description: Only as wide as the content (inline) instead of the full width

components.name: ChatMessage
components.description: A message: author and time (only for screen readers when grouped), the bubble, the delivery status

props.name: text
props.description: Text of the message – Markdown unless `markdown` is false (children replace it)

props.name: markdown
props.description: Render the text as Markdown (default true); otherwise plain text with its line breaks

props.name: author
props.description: Name of the author, above the message

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar image (default: the initials of the author)

props.name: time
props.description: Time sent: ISO text, timestamp or Date (shown as the time of day)

props.name: status
props.description: Delivery status of an own message: sending, sent, read, error (shown as icon and text)

props.name: attachments
props.description: Files of the message: name and size, a tap opens them

props.name: onAttachmentPress
props.description: A tap on an attachment (default: opens its `href` with Linking)

props.name: align
props.description: start (others, default), end (own messages) or center (system notes)

props.name: grouped
props.description: Follows a message of the same author: avatar and name only for screen readers

props.name: streaming
props.description: The text is still being written: a cursor while it grows, aria-busy until it is complete

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of `#` in the Markdown (default 3)

props.name: children
props.description: Own content instead of the text

props.name: before
props.description: Above the bubble, e.g. ChatThinking or ChatToolCall

props.name: after
props.description: Below the bubble, e.g. ChatSources

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons next to the status (copy, retry …)

components.name: ChatMessages
components.description: Message list: an inverted FlatList (newest at the bottom) with date lines and grouped messages. It is no live region – new messages of others are announced, streamed ones once complete; aria-busy while a reply is written. Scrolled up, a button leads to the new messages; the top loads older ones.

props.name: messages
props.description: The messages, oldest first

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the list (default "Messages")

props.name: groupWithin
props.description: Messages of the same author within this many minutes are grouped (default 5)

props.name: separators
props.description: A date line before the first message of each day (default true)

props.name: now
props.description: Today's date – the date lines then say "Today" and "Yesterday"

props.name: markdown
props.description: Message texts are Markdown (default true)

props.name: announce
props.description: Announces new messages of others – streamed ones once they are complete (default true)

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Older messages can be loaded: reaching the top (or the button there) calls onLoadMore

props.name: loading
props.description: Older messages are loading

props.name: onLoadMore
props.description: Load older messages (they are added at the top, the view stays where it is)

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Text without messages

props.name: renderMessage
props.description: A message (default: ChatMessage)

props.name: onAttachmentPress
props.description: A tap on an attachment of a message (default: opens its `href` with Linking)

components.name: ChatPrompt
components.description: Prompt of a chat: a text field that grows up to `maxRows` lines, attached files with a remove button each, a send button – and a stop button instead while a reply is written.

props.name: value
props.description: The text (controlled)

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the field (default "Message")

props.name: responding
props.description: A reply is being written: the send button becomes a stop button (calls onStop)

props.name: attachments
props.description: A button to attach files from the `pickers`

props.name: pickers
props.description: Sources of attachments: documentPicker() from `@wirecore/wirelayer-native/expo-document-picker`, imageLibraryPicker() … or own – several open a choice

props.name: files
props.description: Attached files (controlled)

props.name: accept
props.description: Accepted file types for attachments, passed to the pickers, e.g. ["image/*", "application/pdf"]

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Lines the field grows to before it scrolls (default 8)

props.name: sendOn
props.description: Web with a hardware keyboard: `enter` (default) sends with Enter, Shift+Enter adds a line; `mod-enter` sends with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. On iOS and Android only the send button sends (Enter adds a line).

props.name: hint
props.description: Web: shows how to send and add a line (default true)

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Send: the text (trimmed) and the attached files; the field is cleared afterwards

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop the reply that is being written

components.name: ChatSources
components.description: Sources of an answer: a button (aria-expanded) that shows a list of links with their host names

props.name: title
props.description: Text of the button (default "3 sources")

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open at first

props.name: onLinkPress
props.description: A tap on a source (default: Linking.openURL)

components.name: ChatThinking
components.description: The reasoning of an answer: collapsed by default, "Thinking …" while it is being written

props.name: active
props.description: Still thinking: "Thinking …" with a spinner, aria-busy

props.name: text
props.description: The reasoning (plain text; children replace it)

props.name: duration
props.description: Seconds it took – shown when done

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open at first

components.name: ChatToolCall
components.description: A tool call of an assistant: name and status on the button (aria-expanded), arguments and result inside

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the tool, e.g. "Get weather"

props.name: status

props.name: input
props.description: Arguments of the call (objects are shown as JSON)

props.name: output
props.description: Result of the call (objects are shown as JSON)

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open at first

props.name: children
props.description: More content inside

props.name: value
props.description: Value inside a CheckboxGroup – the group holds the state

props.name: children

components.description: A large card that is one checkbox: title (name), description and price (description), icon

props.name: title
props.description: Title – the accessible name of the control

props.name: description
props.description: Text below the title – read as the description

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon component at the start

props.name: price

props.name: children
props.description: More content below the description

props.name: value
props.description: Value inside a CheckboxGroup (the group holds the state)

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled state (alone; in a CheckboxGroup the group holds the value)

components.description: A named group (role "group") of checkboxes or checkbox cards; helper and error text describe it

props.name: error

props.name: required

props.name: columns

props.name: children

components.name: Chip
components.description: A compact label with optional icon or image and a remove button (44 pt touch area) – e.g. a chosen filter

props.name: label
props.description: Text of the chip (or the children); also names its remove button

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon component before the label

props.name: avatar

props.name: removable

components.name: ChipGroup

props.name: multiple

props.name: label
props.description: Name of the group, e.g. "Filter locations"

props.name: language

props.description: File name in the header; also sets the language when `language` is not given

props.name: lineNumbers

props.name: highlightLines

props.description: Copy button in the header (default true): calls `onCopy` – e.g. `copy` of `useClipboard()` from `@wirecore/wirelayer-native/expo-clipboard`; without `onCopy` only the web copies (navigator.clipboard)

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Copies the code (the app's clipboard) – the button announces "Copied to clipboard"

props.name: header

props.name: maxHeight

props.description: With `maxHeight`: the code is cut off there and a button shows all of it

props.name: wrap

props.name: defaultWrap
props.description: Wrapping at the start (uncontrolled)

props.name: wrapToggle
props.description: A button in the header switches line wrapping

props.name: diff
props.description: Marks lines starting with "+" as added and "-" as removed (e.g. a patch)

props.name: addedLines
props.description: Added lines (1-based)

props.name: removedLines
props.description: Removed lines (1-based)

props.name: languages
props.description: More grammars than the built-in ones (Shiki registrations or loaders, e.g. `() => import('shiki/langs/ruby.mjs')`) – their licence is the responsibility of the app

props.name: swatches

props.name: withPicker

props.name: aria-label

props.name: items
props.description: The colours to choose from

props.name: value
props.description: Chosen colour (its value, controlled)

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label of the group (default "Color")

props.name: showLabels
props.description: Shows the names below the swatches (otherwise only for screen readers)

props.name: renderValue

props.name: emptyText

components.description: Data table for phones and tablets, without a table library: a table that scrolls sideways (sort by tapping a header) or one card per row (`layout`, automatic below `cardsBelow`). In the web build the table is a complete ARIA table; on iOS and Android every row is a named group and every cell is read with its header.
